signed_reason: I ran and reviewed the CPMB load-budget evaluation: gate behaviour 42/42, published-text checks 29/29, machinery 56/56. A first run failed 12 of these; every failure was a real defect and every one was fixed rather than waived — two regulators specced to drop out on a rail other than the one their own target state names (duplicated verbatim into Appendix D), brownout volts that contradicted Chapter 14's own normalized band and hysteresis rule, a sequencer gate in Chapter 14 that released Operational on Principled alone, an answer key contradicting its own chapter, a published recipe that could not compile because a Drive was glossed with '|' where '|' introduces the Register, and a code board that did not match the published one. GAPS REMAIN AND ARE RECORDED, NOT CLOSED: the additive energy budget (rail capacity, summed draw, time-to-brownout) has no implementation, no overcommit predicate exists in the repository, and beta-scale derates are not enforced. SCOPE: the gates that exist, and consistency of the published text. This does NOT establish that a load budget is enforced at runtime.
